reaction: The connection between the lining, fluid and gliding surfaces is clear.
reason: Add the ligaments to support the elbow; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a supported elbow joint that can still move, completing the remaining goal.

effect: The ligaments complete the supported elbow, allowing bending while resisting sideways movement; all chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The arrows make the distinction between movement and restraint clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the mineralised framework with supplied bone cells brought the separate components together in a living-bone cutaway. The preceding contrast between collagen and mineral also explained their different structural roles.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding cartilage was straightforward, but the result repeated the expected smooth caps and sliding rather than adding much beyond that connection.

surprise.text: The distinction between blood vessels and the tiny fluid-filled channels carrying nutrients toward embedded osteocytes sharpened my understanding of how living bone is supplied.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though linking bone cells directly to blood vessels was a simplified construction; the result clarified the nutrient pathway. The compatible menu supplied the pairing rather than requiring me to discover it.

continue.text: I would continue: assembling the elbow connected its lining, fluid, cartilage and ligaments to movement and restraint, making me curious about how muscles would move it.
